notes: THE FIRST GENUINELY INDEPENDENT REVIEW IN THIS REPOSITORY. Thirteen records precede it; every one was written by a subagent of its own author, and nine did not say so. This reviewer was dispatched by a DIFFERENT SESSION (a peer session's orchestrator, session token 3b64530b), working read-only in its own scratch clone. Its text is reproduced as it wrote it; the dispatching orchestrator's only edit was replacing one local clone path with <path>, which that orchestrator disclosed unprompted. VERDICT, in the reviewer's words: 'As a report-only gate it is sound. When nothing is checked it says so, both in words and with its own exit code (2, separate from 0). I found no case where it reports success after checking nothing. There are four defects, none of which blocks a report-only merge. Three have to be fixed before this gate is made blocking. Finding 5 is a set of false claims in the PR description.' It cloned the repo, checked out ab0f875, confirmed it matched gh pr view headRefOid, and called reexecute_verifiable_commands directly with fabricated records, letting each command really run. THE FOUR REQUESTED CASES ALL HELD: all-false gives '0 of 1 -- NOTHING WAS RE-EXECUTED, THIS PROVES NOTHING' at exit 2; an empty commands array gives '0 of 0' at exit 2, and the schema requires at least one command anyway; a differing sanitiser_version gives UNCOMPARABLE naming both versions; a recorded lwb_check_proof.py gives SKIPPED-SELF. Also holding: a missing sha256 FAILs, a missing exit FAILs, a string 'true' for verifiable is not run, and the real head run gives 4 of 107 across 13 records, all matched, exit 0. FIVE FINDINGS, every one reproduced by the author before acting. (1) UNCOMPARABLE commands count toward neither failures nor the re-executed total, so one real pass beside a drifted command still prints the success summary at exit 0 -- a sanitiser version bump could render every historical digest uncomparable while the gate still exits 0. (2) Empty output and expected errors pass by design: a command printing nothing matches the empty-string hash, and a command recorded with exit 1 passes when it exits 1. The gate proves output reproduces, not that a command checks anything; the reviewer judged the PR's own '4 of 107 ... must never be described as more than that' framing honest about this. (3) THE RECURSION GUARD IS BYPASSABLE, confirmed: _command_resolves_to_self compares the exact filename case-sensitively, so LWB_CHECK_PROOF.PY, 'python -m lwb_check_proof', a bash -c wrapper and a subprocess.run wrapper all escape it -- the uppercase form was observed actually re-executing rather than being skipped. With no subprocess timeout anywhere, a wrapped self-call carrying --reexecute would not terminate and would stall a CI job even under continue-on-error. (4) A verifiable command with no argv crashes the run with a TypeError, because --reexecute validates no records and catches only OSError; loud and never mistakable for a pass, but unvalidated. (5) THE PR DESCRIPTION WAS FALSE IN FOUR PLACES, and this is the finding that matters most about the process rather than the code: it claimed 3 of 101 across 12 records and a live digest mismatch when the head produces 4 of 107 across 13, all matched; it claimed only proof/20.json carried the flag when proof/21.json carries two verifiable commands; and it claimed 351 tests when the suite is 364. THREE SUBAGENT REVIEW PASSES READ THAT DESCRIPTION AND NONE CAUGHT IT. The first independent reviewer caught it immediately. The description is corrected and now names which of its own claims were wrong. DISPOSITION: findings 1, 3 and 4 are recorded in the PR body as defects that MUST be fixed before this gate is ever made blocking -- a separate PR that also requires evidence that digests reproduce on a Linux runner. They are deliberately not fixed inside this PR: it is report-only, none can cause a false pass in that mode, and this repo has twice lost a PR to unbounded scope. The reviewer's judgement that they do not block a report-only merge is relied upon here and recorded as the reviewer's, not the author's. NOT CHECKED, in the reviewer's words: Linux or runner reproduction of the digests and the CI run itself; the test suite, which it did not run; the pr-authority rename and modify logic; whether each of the 'four ways' tests fails without its guard; and arbitrary argv in a PR's proof record running in CI, noted only since CI already runs the PR's own code.
